sample_unit: EEG records (mean 67 hours each; 4,036 hours total)
models_evaluated: REMI Vigilenz AI for Event Detection (VED)

links.outcome: VED and Persyst 15 sensitivity and false positives per day versus expert epileptologists on same EEG records
links.effect: VED averaged sensitivity 77.0% [69.4-83.2] with 4.79 FPs/day; P15 65.4% [56.0-74.0] with 1.30 FPs/day; VED non-inferior in sensitivity but not FPs/day at Low confidence.
links.quote: VED at the official Low confidence level demonstrated non-inferiority in sensitivity (p < 0.01), while not meeting statistical non-inferiority for FPs/day.

links.outcome: Inter-rater agreement among expert epileptologists defining the seizure reference standard
links.effect: Relative inter-rater sensitivity between experts ranged from 68.4% to 88.3%; relative FPs/day ranged from 0.16 to 0.79, showing experts disagree on what constitutes a seizure.
links.quote: Relative inter-rater sensitivity between the experts ranged from 68.4% (95% confidence interval [CI[Formula: see text]]=[48.8%, 84.5%]) to 88.3%, [77.5%, 94.7%], while relative FPs/day ranged from 0.16, [0.02, 0.47] to 0.79, [0.14, 2.48].

unlisted_practices: Inter-rater agreement evaluation paradigm rather than consensus reference for validating seizure detection
Evaluating on complete multiday EEG recordings rather than preselected snippets

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates the performance and inter-rater agreement of a commercial AI tool for reduced-channel EEG seizure detection against expert epileptologists and full-channel software, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
